title: Does light fine-tuning (LoRA) break the link between a safety vector and the behavior it controls?

original_idea.body: Extract a safety vector on a base model; apply to a public/tiny LoRA fine-tune and measure effectiveness erosion, plus whether re-extraction recovers; single consumer GPU.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if steering doesn't transfer to community LoRA fine-tunes, base-model safety claims fail downstream (level 4).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Extract vector + apply to a LoRA fine-tune (or train a tiny LoRA); guided (level 4).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped with clear success criterion (effectiveness drop on fine-tune) (level 5).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Community LoRA transfer is lab-deprioritized; neglected open-weight safety work (level 5).

low_compute.reasoning: Optional tiny LoRA training + inference; single consumer GPU, mid-range.

novelty.reasoning: LoRA-specific community-framed steering transfer appears mostly novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: LoRA-specific steering transfer appears mostly novel.
